written.myAnswer: A force can change the speed (magnitude) of an object's velocity, its direction, or both.
It will continue moving with constant velocity indefinitely, provided no net force acts on it.
Newton's first law cannot be demonstrated perfectly on Earth because friction and other forces cannot be completely eliminated; these forces affect an object's motion.
Because of inertia, your body tends to remain at rest as the car accelerates forward, so you appear to be pushed back into the seat.
The acceleration is determined by the resultant (net) force on the body. Balanced forces have zero resultant and produce no acceleration.

The action and reaction act on different bodies, so they do not cancel each other on either body. The ground exerts a forward frictional force on the horse; if this force is sufficient to overcome opposing forces, the horse-cart system accelerates.

First law: A body remains at rest or continues in uniform motion in a straight line unless acted on by a net external force. Second law: The acceleration is in the direction of the net force and is proportional to that force and inversely proportional to the body's mass; F = ma. Third law: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
